intro: You're looking for a fleet insurance broker near you because you have several business vehicles to cover and want someone local who understands the practicalities. A broker can compare policies, explain what's included and help you manage the cover as your fleet changes. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a fleet insurance broker usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for a fleet insurance broker near them are trying to make sense of covering multiple vehicles without losing track of the details.
needs: You run a small business with a handful of vans or cars and want them on one policy rather than renewing each separately.
Your fleet has grown beyond the threshold where a standard motor policy works, and you need a broker who understands fleet cover.
You want to know how different insurers treat drivers who aren't named on the policy, such as occasional staff or new hires.
You're considering telematics to help monitor driving and would like advice on whether it could suit your fleet.
You need a broker who can explain exclusions clearly and be on hand if you ever need to make a claim.
context_heading: Why 'near me' matters for fleet insurance
context: Fleet insurance brokers can work remotely, but many businesses prefer someone nearby for face-to-face meetings and a better understanding of local risks. A nearby broker may also be more familiar with the type of vehicles and routes common in your area.

Fleet size thresholds vary between insurers, so it's worth checking how each defines a fleet. Driver policies also matter: some policies cover any driver, while others list named drivers, and this affects both cover and cost. Telematics can help monitor driving behaviour, but it's not for everyone.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: How many vehicles you need to cover and what types they are, such as vans, cars or a mix.
The main use of the vehicles, for example deliveries, carrying equipment or transporting staff.
Whether you need cover for any driver or only named drivers.
Any claims history or driving convictions for the business or its drivers.
Whether you already use telematics or would consider it.
Your preferred location for a broker near you and whether you want face-to-face meetings.
questions: How do you define a fleet for insurance purposes, and does my number of vehicles qualify?
What is your approach to driver policies, and can you explain the difference between any-driver and named-driver cover?
Which insurers do you work with for fleet insurance, and what are their key exclusions?
How do you handle claims, and what support do you provide if I need to make one?

How are you paid for arranging my policy, and will you tell me in writing?

faqs.q: Do I need a broker who is local to me for fleet insurance?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but a local broker can be convenient for face-to-face meetings and may understand local risks better. Many brokers work remotely effectively, so it depends on your preference.

faqs.q: What is the difference between fleet insurance and standard motor insurance?
faqs.a: Fleet insurance covers several vehicles under one policy, which can simplify administration and sometimes reduce cost. Standard motor insurance typically covers one vehicle per policy.

faqs.q: Can I include different types of vehicles in a fleet policy?
faqs.a: Many fleet policies can cover a mix of vehicle types, such as vans and cars, but this depends on the insurer. A broker can check which insurers will cover your specific mix.

faqs.q: How can I check that a broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check on the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) register. Brokers must be authorised by the FCA or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm.

extra_heading: How fleet cover differs from insuring each vehicle separately
extra: With separate motor policies, each vehicle has its own renewal date, its own excess and its own set of terms, which is easy to lose track of once you are running more than a couple of vehicles. A fleet policy brings them together under one arrangement, so there is a single renewal to diarise and one set of documents to keep on top of. That is often the practical reason people start searching for a fleet insurance broker near them rather than simply renewing as before.

The trade-off is that fleet cover is not automatically cheaper or broader. Insurers set their own thresholds for what counts as a fleet, and the driver terms vary considerably, so a policy that suits a business with named drivers may not suit one that lets staff drive pool vehicles. A broker's job is to set out those differences plainly and explain the exclusions that tend to catch people out, such as how vehicles are used or who is permitted to drive them.

It also helps to think about what happens mid-policy, not just at renewal. Adding a vehicle, taking one off the road or changing a regular driver are routine events for a growing business, and how straightforward those changes are depends on the insurer and the broker handling them. Ask at the outset how changes and claims are managed, and who you would speak to.

extra_faqs.q: Will moving to a fleet policy save my business money?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Bringing vehicles under one policy can reduce administration and may help on cost, but it depends on your vehicles, drivers and claims history. A broker can compare what is available and explain the figures rather than promise a saving.

extra_faqs.q: Can I add or remove a vehicle during the year?
extra_faqs.a: Usually yes, but the terms differ between insurers, and some changes may affect your premium. It is worth asking how mid-term adjustments are handled before you choose a policy.

extra_faqs.q: What should I have ready before speaking to a broker?
extra_faqs.a: A list of the vehicles and their registrations, who drives them and how they are used, plus any claims history, will let the conversation get straight to the point. It also helps to say whether you would consider telematics.
